- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% relative to recent history.
- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33), model tends to overreact with upward bias; dampen forecast growth by 10–15% in such periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 5–10% downward correction to subsequent forecasts.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — forecasts drift toward historical mean after 10–15 days; adjust for diminishing momentum in later forecast days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model underestimates downward moves; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing short-term volatility; add 1–2% smoothing to reduce overreaction to recent sentiment shifts.
